transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-11 15:00 PDT — Duration: 60m
Attendees: Alex Monroe, Priya Shah, Daniel Park (Redwood) — Maya Lopez, Ravi Desai, Ellen Kim, Samir Patel (Inkwell)

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining our QBR for Inkwell — appreciate you taking the time. we'll walk through usage, costs, any reliability incidents and recommended next steps.
00:12 Maya: Thanks Alex. quick note — we had a spike in false positives last month tied to a model drift, so want to go deeper on runway and rollback plans.
00:25 Priya: yes and also want to confirm data retention and logs for audit purposes, Ellen mentioned procurement needed the SOC2 artifacts.
00:40 Daniel: for context, we looked at your token distribution and see heavy tail on sequence length — that's driving KV cache misses and extra latency. a few clarifying q's: are most of those long requests synchronous user-facing or async batch?
00:55 Ravi: mostly sync for the fraud UI, about 20% are >1k tokens during investigations. the rest is batch scoring.
01:10 Alex: ok that helps. on cost — your avg tokens/month is about 320M and rising 15% q/q, cost center shows spikes on analytical days. we recommended a reserved pool for peak windows to smooth unit cost.
01:30 Samir: talk through dedicated vs hosted — we need predictable latency and data isolation, but don't want to overcommit for low months. what are burst options?
01:45 Daniel: Dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and private tenancy. Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscale policies; we typically configure a baseline commit and burst buffer. if you want to avoid overcommit, a mixed routing policy (hosted fallback) works — but that changes RPO for some requests.
02:05 Maya: any tradeoffs for quantization? we heard lower cost but potential quality loss for sensitive scoring models.
02:18 Daniel: yes quantization (4-bit/8-bit) helps cost a lot, but for high-stakes fraud scoring we recommend an eval set — we can propose quant configs per model. we'll include a regression matrix in the follow-up.
02:35 Priya: on security — Ellen, you had a provisioning question on SAML and KMS?
02:42 Ellen: procurement wants to confirm KMS key access model and audit logs retention. do you support customer-managed keys and HSM?
02:52 Alex: we support KMS integrations and can show the HSM options in Private deployments. Redwood Private has customer-controlled key access and full audit exports. we'll share the network diagram and audit sample.
03:05 Ravi: our infra team also needs to understand VPC peering and whether the control plane touches PII.
03:12 Priya: short answer — for Private we can run a customer-controlled control plane, for Dedicated we provide strong isolation and audit logs, hosted keeps metadata for routing but is SOC2 compliant. we'll get you detailed separation docs.
03:28 Samir: curious about reliability — we saw a 20-min outage in April; can you walk through root cause and mitigations?
03:38 Daniel: that incident was due to a kernel upgrade on GPU hosts and a mis-scheduled canary rollout; primary mitigation now is automated rollback on model-serving config mismatch, and improved canary gating. since then we've added a fallback to smaller model variant to preserve availability.
03:58 Maya: how does caching help with tail latency? we rely on prefix matches for common flows but not for investigation flows.
04:08 Daniel: prefix/KV caching works best when you have repeated prompts; for long unique investigative prompts we rely on batching and optimized kernels. we can tune your batching window to reduce p99 while keeping p50 low.
04:28 Alex: pricing note — with reserved capacity you can cut unit costs ~30% at your scale but you trade commit. we'll propose 3 sizing options in the follow-up.
04:40 Ellen: procurement asks that any contract include SLAs around latency and uptime plus credits for breaches.
04:48 Alex: we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers on Dedicated; we can surface exact terms in the commercial packet.
05:00 Maya: roadmap — we're most interested in better observability for per-route token costs and an easier way to pin model versions for audits.
05:10 Priya: Redwood Console already supports per-route dashboards and trace hooks; we'll demo an audit-runbook and the model pinning workflow in the technical deep-dive.
05:24 Ravi: last Q — do you have examples of customers running high-throughput scoring with similar p99 targets?
05:30 Daniel: yes, we've benchmarked in finance workloads — we'll share the anonymized benchmark sheet.
05:40 Alex: ok let's recap next steps and owners. thanks everyone.
05:50 Maya: thanks all.

End of transcript.
